description: odo-sliding's rule met at the one declared maximum where a table can be mistaken for an ordinary group: OCCURS 0 TO 1 TIMES DEPENDING ON, read odoslide, in a variable-length dataset. The group is present in a record or it is absent from it, and the item behind it begins at the byte after the last occurrence the count states -- which, on a record whose count is zero, is the byte after the count itself. Three records, of no occurrence, one and none again, so the absence is met twice and is data rather than a constant. What the entry is here to catch is a consumer that asks whether an item repeats by reading the copybook's declared maximum alone: at a maximum of one that answer is no, the group is read unconditionally, and OPT-TEXT is taken out of the four bytes belonging to OPT-TAIL on two of these three records -- which then runs off the end of a five-byte record rather than returning a wrong value, so the framing is what reports it. The pair with odo-sliding is the point: one rule, two maxima, and nothing in either file to disagree with a reader that has only ever seen the other.
source: docs/ir/SPEC.md, "A variable record is a sum with a variable term", "An item after a table slides, and the other reading is a fixed table", "A variable record does not fit a fixed-length dataset", "A count is in hand before the extent it decides"; docs/conformance/GRAMMAR.md, `table-none`
